what.text: GHRP-2, also called pralmorelin, is a lab-made growth hormone-releasing peptide. FDA notes it contains an amino acid not found in nature. It acts on the ghrelin receptor in the pituitary to release growth hormone.

src.label: FDA, bulk drug substances that may present significant safety risks (Category 2 page)
Raun et al., Eur J Endocrinol, 1998

what.text: In Japan, pralmorelin hydrochloride was approved on October 22, 2004 as GHRP Kaken 100 (Kaken Pharmaceutical), a diagnostic agent used to test how well the body secretes growth hormone. It is a one-time test, not a treatment.

src.label: PMDA, List of Approved Drugs, April 2004 to February 2026

what.text: In pigs it released growth hormone and also raised the stress hormones ACTH and cortisol.

src.label: Raun et al., Eur J Endocrinol, 1998

what.text: GHRP-2 is not FDA approved. Its only approval we found is in Japan, as a diagnostic test. Using it for sleep is off-label wherever it is approved, and has barely been studied.

research.text: GHRP-2 has been studied in people mainly as a one-dose test for growth hormone deficiency, and as an infusion in patients in intensive care. The one sleep study we found, in seven healthy men, found no effect on deep sleep.
Each study is listed below as it was run.

src.label: PubMed search for 'GHRP-2 sleep'
ClinicalTrials.gov search for 'GHRP-2'

research.title: Late-night injection in young men, 1998

facts.v: GHRP-2 or saline by vein in random order, given during sleep after the third REM period

research.found: Growth hormone and prolactin rose. Apart from a non-significant tendency to more wakefulness in the first hour, sleep did not change. There was no increase in deep (slow-wave) sleep, unlike what is seen with GHRH.

src.label: Moreno-Reyes et al., Am J Physiol, 1998

research.text: Growth hormone testing (the approved use in Japan)

research.title: GHRP-2 test in adults, 2007

facts.v: one 100 microgram dose by vein after an overnight fast, compared with the insulin tolerance test
77 healthy people and 58 patients with growth hormone deficiency

research.found: Peak growth hormone averaged 84.6 micrograms per litre in healthy people and 1.36 in patients. The authors proposed a cut-off of 15 to tell them apart.

src.label: Chihara et al. (KP-102 Study Group), Eur J Endocrinol, 2007

research.text: Japan, 2013: in 71 adults with pituitary tumors, the GHRP-2 test was compared with the insulin tolerance test and the arginine test. The authors found it an acceptable alternative for diagnosing adult growth hormone deficiency in Japanese patients.

src.label: Kinoshita et al., Endocr J, 2013

research.title: Long-term critical illness, 1999

facts.v: 5 days of placebo and 5 days of GHRP-2 plus TRH by continuous infusion, in random order
14 patients (mean age 68) critically ill for about 40 days
growth and thyroid hormones, markers of protein and bone breakdown

research.found: Growth hormone, IGF-1 and thyroid hormones rose toward normal, and some markers shifted toward building tissue. Cortisol did not change.

src.label: Van den Berghe et al., J Clin Endocrinol Metab, 1999

research.text: 2002: 33 men with prolonged critical illness were randomly assigned to 5 days of placebo, GHRP-2 alone, GHRP-2 plus TRH, or both plus GnRH. GHRP-2 restored growth hormone release and normalized IGF-1; only the three-drug combination raised testosterone.

src.label: Van den Berghe et al., Clin Endocrinol (Oxf), 2002

us.text: Not FDA approved for any use. FDA placed GHRP-2 for injection and nasal use in Category 2 for outsourcing facilities (503B) on September 29, 2023, because it may present significant safety risks. As of November 1, 2026.

items.text: none. A search of Drugs@FDA found no product with pralmorelin as an active ingredient.

items.text: GHRP-2 for injectable and nasal routes was added on September 29, 2023. FDA says these products may pose a risk of immune reactions, and that it "is aware of reports of serious adverse [events] in patients who received GHRP-2, including increased insulin requirement to maintain the blood glucose level, death of critically ill study subjects, infection and pancreatitis, though causality has not been established."

us.text: Compounded drugs are not FDA-approved. FDA does not review their safety, effectiveness or quality before they are sold. Using GHRP-2 for sleep would be off-label anywhere it is approved.

world.lead: GHRP-2 is approved in Japan only, as a diagnostic test for growth hormone secretion. It is not approved in the US, and no product was found in Canada or the EU. Australia makes it prescription-only, and WADA bans it at all times.

countries.status: Not approved. Injectable and nasal GHRP-2 in FDA's compounding Category 2 for outsourcing facilities (503B) since Sept 29, 2023.

after.text: GHRP-2 (pralmorelin) is prohibited at all times (in and out of competition) under WADA class S2.2.4, growth hormone releasing factors. The class names "GH-releasing peptides (GHRPs) [e.g. alexamorelin, examorelin (hexarelin), GHRP-1, GHRP-2 (pralmorelin), GHRP-3, GHRP-4, GHRP-5 and GHRP-6]." All substances in class S2 are non-Specified. It is still named in the same class on the 2027 list, which takes effect January 1, 2027.
